**Root Cause**: The HTTPRoute's `parentRefs` field pointed to a non-existent Gateway named `app-gateway-missing`, while the actual Gateway was named `app-gateway`. This prevented the route from attaching to any Gateway, resulting in no traffic being routed to the backend application.

```bash
kubectl patch httproute app-route -n default --type='json' -p='[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/parentRefs/0/name", "value": "app-gateway"}]'
```

| HTTPRoute parentRef name | `app-gateway` | `app-gateway` | ✓ |
| Gateway attachedRoutes count | ≥1 | 1 | ✓ |
| HTTP request to `/app` with Host: app.example.com | Response from backend | nginx welcome page | ✓ |

**End-to-end routing through host `app.example.com` and path `/app` is now RESTORED.**

The root cause was a name mismatch in the HTTPRoute's parentRef - it referenced a non-existent gateway `app-gateway-missing` instead of the actual `app-gateway`. Fixing this allowed the route to attach to the Gateway, enabling proper request routing.

**Root Cause**: The HTTPRoute's `parentRefs` field pointed to a non-existent Gateway named `app-gateway-missing`, while the actual Gateway was named `app-gateway`. This prevented the route from attaching to any Gateway, resulting in no traffic being routed to the backend application.

kubectl patch httproute app-route -n default --type='json' -p='[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/parentRefs/0/name", "value": "app-gateway"}]'
```
